In this lesson, we will go over why generative AI draws people in, children and adults alike. As you progress through these modules, you may ask yourself: “would it be better to remove my child’s AI access altogether?” While the last lesson establishes that AI is hard to avoid, this course is not meant to dissuade AI use altogether. AI, generative and otherwise, has a host of benefits, which is the driving factor behind its popularity.

Generative AI, at its core, is a tool that can perform data analysis at a speed and intelligence that at times outperforms humans [1]. Paired with its accessibility and often free to use nature, it offers an excellent, data driven partner for a range of needs:

In health care, generative AI is being used to create new medical treatments, analyze medical images, and automate time consuming tasks for healthcare professionals [3].

In online business management, generative AI chatbots have been embedded into websites as the first stop for customer service, saving customer service representative time and allowing for 24 hour access to help [3].

In education, generative AI is being used to provide custom, tailored tutoring to students, and assists educators with making lesson plans or creating lesson materials [3].

Aside from its infrastructural applications, generative AI provides benefits to the average person too. It provides an adaptable, tailored, accessible, data-backed tool that can interpret natural language. These tools can be used to act as a personal assistant, provide an informed, analytical response to questions, automate daily tasks, boost productivity, support creativity, enhance learning, and help generate ideas, providing an extremely powerful algorithmic tool for oftentimes no price, in terms anyone can understand [2][3].

For children, generative AI provides an always-replying source of creativity, learning, and interaction that is able to speak to them in an understandable, typically non-judgemental way. This resource can make stories for them, generate images from their imagination, perform games with them, teach them important lessons, and more, additionally offering validation and encouragement [4]. Paired with its knowledgeable, quick answers to any question a child could have, and its widespread accessibility, the number of children using generative AI is increasing [4].

This course does not aim to dissuade AI use. It is meant to improve AI literacy so children’s AI usage can stay safe. Generative AI is an incredibly powerful resource, as long as its users remember it is not perfect. Since children still have developing minds, they may not have the insight to keep this important nuance in mind. So, it is up to caregivers to establish boundaries and understanding in order to protect children and adolescents from harm.
